rules.description: Every open non-draft PR behind main gets a silent branch refresh with the workflow token (pushes trigger no workflows, so freshness is free); validating PRs are excluded so the validation head never moves mid-run. mergeState matches BEHIND or BLOCKED — REST mergeable_state flip-flops between the two for the same behind PR under branch protection, and gh pr update-branch is a no-op on a fresh branch, so over-matching is harmless. Replaces the retired auto-update-prs workflow.
GitHub PR: merge window — oldest armed PR gets a PAT update (validation CI fires on the final head) + ai_validating marker (#687)
GitHub PR: validation CI red on the final head -> unarm, report, requeue agent:rework on the linked issue (#687). NB: labels are OR-matched; ai_validating only ever lands on armed (pr_approved) PRs.
GitHub PR: validation green + CLEAN -> squash-merge, clear markers (FIFO drain, #687). NB: labels are OR-matched; ai_validating implies armed (pr_approved).

Validated-but-stale: armed (ai_validating) + validation concluded but base moved before the merge tick. silent-update-behind excludes ai_validating and merge-validated needs CLEAN, so without this unarm the PR deadlocks (live: fa pr-744). Drops ai_validating; the silent refresh + merge window re-validate the fresh head (the 422-arm covers the already-fresh case), then merge fires.

Auto rework leg: agent:rework armed on the issue either by the review verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED) or by red pre-merge CI. Pushing fixes removes the label (pr_rework removeLabels). prMachineAuthor: auto rework fires ONLY on machine-authored PRs (owner rule) — the machine login is deployment config (jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor / factory-sm machine-author input), never hardcoded; unconfigured fails closed. Manual rework on ANY PR: label the PR agent:rework (see rework-on-label).

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework (red CI or review CHANGES)

rules.description: Manual rework request: agent:rework label on the PR itself -> rework on demand, ANY author (a human asked explicitly). Dispatches the issue-anchored rework leg on the linked issue (closing-keyword/#N body reference); the PR label is consumed on dispatch so the next tick does not re-fire. PRs without a linked issue are skipped loudly.

inputs.reason: sm: agent:rework label on the PR (manual rework request)

rules.description: Machine-loop completion backfill: an open issue with an open+green MACHINE-authored PR gets ai_developed, which arms review-after-dev. Machine-only (prMachineAuthor) so external PRs never enter the review loop through the backfill; no `in progress` requirement — issues whose dev leg predates the status-label convention (live: fa #503 / PR #676) must still be picked up. Idempotent: ai_developed in notLabels.
GitHub: green PR after dev → machine review (never on an armed PR: pr_approved means the review already concluded APPROVED - re-dispatching review duplicates the leg and un-arms the merge queue)

GitHub PR: external (non-machine) green PR -> one-time review (PR-anchored; no re-review on later pushes). The machine login is deployment-specific: it arrives via jobParams.machineAuthor / config.machineAuthor (factory-sm input machine-author); with none configured every green PR is reviewable.

inputs.reason: sm: external PR green - one-time review

rules.description: GitHub PR: CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict pinned to an older commit (fixes pushed after the review) + green -> re-arm agent:review. review-on-label dispatches the runner, the runner consumes the label and re-reviews the current head; the fresh verdict's commit_id equals the head, so this never loops.

GitHub PR: all review threads resolved + the last verdict is older than the head (fixes landed and the threads were worked through) + green -> re-arm agent:review. Covers PR #676: the rework resolves threads (the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict dissolves into COMMENTED), so verdict-staleness alone misses it. Convergent: the re-review's verdict lands on the current head and its fresh threads are unresolved until worked.
GitHub PR: agent:review label on a PR -> review on demand (any author; consumed by the review runner)
GitHub: linked PR merged → close the issue (cycle complete)
